question.text: Under Section 15F of the SEBI Act, what is the penalty for a stockbroker's failure to issue contract notes in the prescribed form?

answer.text: Not less than one lakh rupees, up to a maximum of one crore rupees
Not less than five lakh rupees, up to twenty-five crore rupees
A flat penalty of one lakh rupees with no per-day component
Not less than ten lakh rupees, up to ten crore rupees

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 15F(a) prescribes a penalty of not less than one lakh rupees, which may extend to one crore rupees, where a stockbroker fails to issue contract notes in the form specified by the stock exchange. The Trap: Section 15F covers three distinct defaults: 15F(a) failure to issue contract notes (the answer above), 15F(b) failure to deliver securities or make payment within the time specified, and 15F(c) charging brokerage in excess of the prescribed rate. Each carries its own penalty scale, so do not mix them up. Note: The minimum-and-maximum structure (not less than one lakh, up to one crore) is the defining feature of the 15F(a) clause.
